nodes_changed.doc:
Declare that every codec bundle has had its chance to register: each
action still awaited becomes unavailable and its waiters' `unavailable`
callbacks run. A codec registered later is still installed and used by
later dispatches, but it does not revive a failed wait.

which the HTML parser fires only after every deferred and module
script in the document has run or failed to load. That makes a codec
bundle's load or evaluation error observable without a timer.

nodes_changed.doc:
Register a payload codec for an action. The transport then sends the
codec's bytes as the frame payload instead of JSON — used by slices

nodes_changed.name: retainCommand
nodes_changed.signature: retainCommand( action: string, payload: () => unknown, unavailable?: (failure: ActionCodecUnavailable) => void, ): void
nodes_changed.doc:
Hold the latest intent for `action` and send it once the action's
codec is registered, then again after every session synchronization
(route initialization repeats on reconnect, RFD-fd0t8b1v). One sender
per action: a later call replaces the payload and failure handler
rather than adding another, so a reconnect re-sends the command once
however many times it was retained. A call made while the codec is
ready and the session synchronized also sends at once.

`payload` is read at send time. `unavailable` runs if the codec never
registers (see `closeActionCodecRegistration`), so the caller can leave
its loading state and render the failure instead of waiting forever.

nodes_changed.name: whenActionCodec
nodes_changed.signature: whenActionCodec( action: string, ready: () => void, unavailable?: (failure: ActionCodecUnavailable) => void, ): void
nodes_changed.doc:
Run `ready` once a payload codec for `action` is registered: now if it
already is, otherwise the instant `registerActionCodec` installs it.
If codec registration closes first (see `closeActionCodecRegistration`)
`unavailable` runs instead. Exactly one of the two runs, once.

The readiness handshake for an action whose contract has no JSON
fallback. Codec bundles are deferred modules that load on their own
schedule, so a page that dispatches such an action as soon as the
session synchronizes can reach the transport first; the transport then
sends JSON the server refuses, and the command is lost. Gating the
dispatch on this callback orders it after the codec, on every
transport, because the transports read the codec from the bus at send
time.

nodes_changed.name: closeActionCodecsAtDocumentLoad
nodes_changed.signature: function closeActionCodecsAtDocumentLoad(bus: BrowserBus, documentRef?: Document): void
nodes_changed.doc:
Close `bus`'s codec registration once the document has loaded. Codec
bundles are `type="module"` scripts without `async`, which the parser
runs (or fails to fetch) before it fires `DOMContentLoaded`, and they
register through `whenBusReady`, which `publishBusReady` has flushed by
then. So a codec still missing at that event belongs to a bundle that
failed, and every command waiting on it is told so instead of waiting
silently. A bundle loaded with `async` or by a dynamic `import()` after
the event is outside this guarantee and must register before anything
waits on its codec. Call after `publishBusReady`.

node.name: BrowserConnectTransport
node.signature: class BrowserConnectTransport implements TransportLike
node.doc:
ConnectRPC transport — the WebSocket alternative (ADR 0016 Phase 3).

Emulates the duplex socket with two half-duplex RPCs on `SessionService`:
a `Subscribe` server-stream for downstream frames and a unary `Send` for
upstream client frames. The session is authenticated by the HttpOnly
`session-id` cookie (sent automatically on the same-origin fetch), so
`SubscribeRequest.session_id` is left empty — the server derives it.

Frames cross the wire as the same protocol-wire bytes the WebSocket
carries: a control `ServerFrame` wraps the `bus.Envelope` bytes; a
`ClientFrame.frame` is the `[TAG_PROTO, …envelope]` the WS transport also
builds. The envelope/framework field handling mirrors
`BrowserWebSocketTransport.#handleProtoFrame` (kept duplicated rather than
extracted to leave the production WS path untouched; DRY in a follow-up).

node.name: pipeBusEventsToDiagnostics
node.signature: function pipeBusEventsToDiagnostics( bus: BrowserBus, recorder: DiagnosticsRecorder, ): () => void
node.doc:
HARVEST threads B + D — bridge BusEvent stream → DiagnosticEvent
journal.

`bus.tap()` emits a `BusEvent` for every signal write, ingest,
dispatch, island transition, and bus.invoke step. The
`DiagnosticsRecorder` records `DiagnosticEvent`s. This helper
subscribes to taps and pushes the subset that has a journal-side
shape:

- `invoke.start` → `command.dispatched` (thread B)
- `invoke.complete` → `command.resolved` (thread B)
- `island.transition` → `actor.transition` (thread D) — keyed by
the island's `actorId(islandId)`. The bridge tracks per-island
previous phase across calls so it can populate
`fromState`/`toState`. Sessions render "no island reached
`ready` before transport.status hit `synced`" by walking these.

Other BusEvent variants (set, ingest, dispatch, handle) don't have
a DiagnosticEvent counterpart yet — they're observable through
`bus.tap()` directly until the journal grows variants for them.

Returns the unsubscribe handle so callers tear the bridge down on
disposal.
